exercises.heading: Section 6.1 Exercises

problem.paragraph: The domain of vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y} \right)$$ is a set of points $$\left( {x,y} \right)$$ in a plane, and the range of F is a set of what in the plane?

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, determine whether the statement is true or false.

problem.paragraph: Vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \left\langle {3x^{2},1} \right\rangle$$ is a gradient field for both $$\phi_{1}\left( {x,y} \right) = x^{3} + y$$ and $$\phi_{2}\left( {x,y} \right) = y + x^{3} + 100.$$
Vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \frac{\left\langle {y,x} \right\rangle}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}$$ is constant in direction and magnitude on a unit circle.
Vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = \frac{\left\langle {y,x} \right\rangle}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}}$$ is neither a radial field nor a rotation.

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, describe each vector field by drawing some of its vectors.
For the following exercises, find the gradient vector field of each function $$f.$$

solution.paragraph: $$F ( x , y ) = sin ( y ) i + ( x cos y - sin y ) j F ( x , y ) = sin ( y ) i + ( x cos y - sin y ) j$$
$$F ( x , y , z ) = ( 2 x y + y ) i + ( x 2 + x + 2 y z ) j + y 2 k F ( x , y , z ) = ( 2 x y + y ) i + ( x 2 + x + 2 y z ) j + y 2 k$$

problem.paragraph: What is vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y} \right)$$ with a value at $$\left( {x,y} \right)$$ that is of unit length and points toward $$\left( {1,0} \right)?$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, write formulas for the vector fields with the given properties.

problem.paragraph: All vectors are parallel to the x-axis and all vectors on a vertical line have the same magnitude.
All vectors point toward the origin and have constant length.

solution.paragraph: $$F ( x , y ) = - x i - y j x 2 + y 2 F ( x , y ) = - x i - y j x 2 + y 2$$

problem.paragraph: All vectors are of unit length and are perpendicular to the position vector at that point.

Give a formula $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = M(x,y)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + N(x,y)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ for the vector field in a plane that has the properties that $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = 0$$ at $$\left( {0,0} \right)$$ and that at any other point $$\left( {a,b} \right),$$ F is tangent to circle $$x^{2} + y^{2} = a^{2} + b^{2}$$ and points in the clockwise direction with magnitude $$\left. ||\mathbf{F} \right.|| = \sqrt{a^{2} + b^{2}}.$$

solution.paragraph: $$F ( x , y ) = y i - x j F ( x , y ) = y i - x j$$

problem.paragraph: Is vector field $$\textbf{F}(x,y) = {< {P(x,y),Q(x,y)} >} = \left( \sin x + y \right)\textbf{i} + \left( \cos y + x \right)\textbf{j}$$ a gradient field?

Find a formula for vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }(x,y) = M(x,y)\mathbf{ \text{i} } + N(x,y)\mathbf{ \text{j} }$$ given the fact that for all points $$(x,y),$$ F points toward the origin and $$\left. ||\mathbf{F} \right.|| = \frac{10}{x^{2} + y^{2}}.$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, assume that an electric field in the xy-plane caused by an infinite line of charge along the x-axis is a gradient field with potential function $$V\left( {x,y} \right) = c \ln \left( \frac{r_{0}}{\sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}} \right),$$ where $$c > 0$$ is a constant and $$r_{0}$$ is a reference distance at which the potential is assumed to be zero.

problem.paragraph: Find the components of the electric field in the x- and y-directions, where $$\mathbf{ \text{E} }\left( {x,y} \right) = - \text{∇} V\left( {x,y} \right).$$
Show that the electric field at a point in the xy-plane is directed outward from the origin and has magnitude $$\left. ||\mathbf{E} \right.|| = \frac{c}{r}$$ , where $$r = \sqrt{x^{2} + y^{2}}$$ .

solution.paragraph: $$E = c x 2 + y 2 x 2 + y 2 = c x 2 + y 2 = c r E = c x 2 + y 2 x 2 + y 2 = c x 2 + y 2 = c r$$

exercises.paragraph: A flow line (or streamline) of a vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }$$ is a curve $$\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t)$$ such that $$d\mathbf{ \text{r} }/dt = \mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {\mathbf{ \text{r} }(t)} \right).$$ If $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }$$ represents the velocity field of a moving particle, then the flow lines are paths taken by the particle. Therefore, flow lines are tangent to the vector field. For the following exercises, show that the given curve $$\mathbf{ \text{c} }(t)$$ is a flow line of the given velocity vector field $$\mathbf{ \text{F} }\left( {x,y,z} \right).$$

solution.paragraph: $$c ′ ( t ) = ( cos t , - sin t , e - t ) = F ( c ( t ) ) c ′ ( t ) = ( cos t , - sin t , e - t ) = F ( c ( t ) )$$

exercises.paragraph: For the following exercises, let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + y\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ $$\mathbf{ \text{G} } = -y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{H} } = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } - y\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Match F, G, and H with their graphs.

For the following exercises, let $$\mathbf{ \text{F} } = x\mathbf{ \text{i} } + y\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ $$\mathbf{ \text{G} } = -y\mathbf{ \text{i} } + x\mathbf{ \text{j} },$$ and $$\mathbf{ \text{H} } = x\mathbf{ \text{i} }-y\mathbf{ \text{j} }.$$ Match the vector fields in a through d with their graphs.
